queries.query: Why does login fail after a server restore?
How can I resolve API rate limiting and HTTP 429 errors?
Why are webhook deliveries failing with HTTP 503?
How do I fix an SSO audience mismatch?
What should I do when OAuth tokens are rejected after a host patch?

Error Code: NX-AUTH-4017
Title: OAuth token rejected due to clock skew
Symptoms: HTTP 401 despite a token that appears valid; Login failures after VM migration, restore, or host patch
Resolution: Synchronize the application host using NTP, verify time, and restart the authentication worker.

Error Code: NX-API-4292
Title: Tenant API burst rate exceeded
Symptoms: HTTP 429; Intermittent throttling during batch or concurrent requests
Resolution: Reduce concurrency, honor Retry-After, and use exponential backoff with jitter.

Error Code: NX-WEBHOOK-5031
Title: Webhook destination unavailable
Symptoms: Webhook delivery receives HTTP 503; Events remain pending while retries occur
Resolution: Verify destination availability, DNS, TLS, and firewall. Allow retry processing after recovery.

Error Code: NX-NOTIFY-2204
Title: Duplicate ticket notification rule match
Symptoms: Same user receives duplicate email for one ticket event
Resolution: Inspect matching rules and subscriptions; remove the redundant trigger and run a controlled test.

Error Code: NX-SEARCH-3108
Title: Search indexing backlog
Symptoms: Recently created or updated tickets absent from search
Resolution: Inspect worker health and backlog; restart a failed worker before considering an index rebuild.

Error Code: NX-AUTH-4020
Title: SSO audience mismatch
Symptoms: SSO redirect loop; Assertion accepted by IdP but rejected by application
Resolution: Correct the audience value and clear stale sessions.

NEXADESK CLOUD - SEPTEMBER 2026 INCIDENT REPORT
Incident ID: INC-2026-09-06
Status: Resolved
Synthetic training document
SUMMARY
On 2026-09-06, outbound webhook processing was degraded for approximately 42 minutes. Queue depth increased across multiple tenants and some deliveries were delayed.
CUSTOMER IMPACT
Webhook events were accepted by NexaDesk but remained pending longer than normal. Some customer endpoints also returned HTTP 503 during the same period, which complicated initial diagnosis.
ROOT CAUSE
A deployment caused outbound webhook workers to run with an unexpectedly low concurrency limit. This created queue saturation across multiple tenants.
MITIGATION
Operations increased worker capacity, rolled back the affected configuration, and monitored queue age until the backlog drained.
DIAGNOSTIC GUIDANCE
This historical incident should not be assumed to explain every webhook 503. For a current case affecting one customer destination, first verify destination availability, DNS, TLS, firewall behavior, and response latency. Suspect a platform incident when queue growth and failures occur across multiple unrelated tenants.
FOLLOW-UP
Added queue-depth alerts and administration visibility for webhook retry state.

NexaDesk Cloud - Administrator and Integration Guide
Version family: 4.8.x | Synthetic training document

1. OAuth Authentication
NexaDesk validates OAuth access tokens against the configured identity provider. Tokens must contain the
expected issuer and audience claims and must be within the configured clock-skew tolerance. Authentication
failures normally return HTTP 401. For reliable authentication, application hosts and identity-provider
infrastructure should use synchronized time. The default supported clock-skew tolerance is five minutes. If
server time differs significantly, otherwise valid tokens can be rejected. Administrators should verify token
expiration, issuer, audience, and host time before rotating credentials.

NexaDesk Cloud - Administrator and Integration Guide
Version family: 4.8.x | Synthetic training document

2. API Rate Limiting
NexaDesk protects tenant APIs with sustained and burst rate limits. In the 4.8 product family, the standard burst
threshold is 120 requests per minute per tenant unless a tenant-specific policy overrides it. Clients that receive
HTTP 429 should reduce concurrency, respect Retry-After when present, and use exponential backoff with
jitter. Repeated immediate retries can extend throttling and increase load. API keys should not be regenerated
as a first response to rate limiting because rate limits are based on tenant traffic policy rather than key validity.

NexaDesk Cloud - Administrator and Integration Guide
Version family: 4.8.x | Synthetic training document

3. Webhook Delivery
Outbound webhooks are delivered asynchronously. NexaDesk treats HTTP 2xx responses as successful
delivery. HTTP 5xx responses, timeouts, DNS failures, and connection failures are retried according to the
delivery policy. For webhook delivery failures, verify endpoint availability, DNS resolution, TLS validity, firewall
rules, and response latency. A destination returning HTTP 503 indicates that the destination is temporarily
unavailable; inspect the endpoint before assuming an internal NexaDesk outage.

NexaDesk Cloud - Administrator and Integration Guide
Version family: 4.8.x | Synthetic training document

4. Ticket and Email Notifications
Ticket notifications can be sent through email and in-product channels. Duplicate notifications can occur when
overlapping notification rules target the same event or when an automation rule and a manual subscription both
trigger delivery. Administrators should inspect active notification rules, event subscriptions, and automation
history. Disabling all notification services is not recommended because it can hide the configuration problem.

NexaDesk Cloud - Administrator and Integration Guide
Version family: 4.8.x | Synthetic training document

5. Search Index and Reporting
Ticket search is backed by an asynchronous indexing pipeline. Recently created or updated tickets can briefly
lag behind transactional data. Reporting jobs operate independently of ticket search and may use cached
aggregates. If search results are stale for an extended period, inspect indexing worker health and backlog
before rebuilding an index.

NexaDesk Cloud - Administrator and Integration Guide
Version family: 4.8.x | Synthetic training document

6. SSO and Session Behavior
Single sign-on sessions depend on identity-provider assertions and NexaDesk session lifetime settings. A user
repeatedly redirected to login may have an invalid audience, expired assertion, blocked third-party cookie, or
excessive time difference between systems. Do not confuse SSO redirect loops with API token failures: both
involve authentication, but their diagnostic paths differ.

# NexaDesk Cloud 4.8 Release Notes
Synthetic product release notes for RAG experimentation.
## 4.8.0 - API traffic controls
NexaDesk 4.8 introduced per-tenant burst-rate enforcement. Standard tenants may receive HTTP 429 when traffic exceeds 120 requests per minute. Integrations should use exponential backoff, jitter, and `Retry-After` when available.
## 4.8.1 - Authentication worker diagnostics
Authentication logging now records issuer, audience-validation result, and detected server-time offset. The supported clock-skew tolerance remains five minutes. A large time difference can cause valid OAuth tokens to be rejected.
## 4.8.1 - Webhook retry visibility
Administrators can inspect webhook retry state and queue age. HTTP 503 from a destination continues to be treated as a retryable destination failure.
## 4.8.1 - Notification rule editor
The rule editor now warns when two ticket notification rules appear to overlap. Existing duplicate rules are not automatically removed.
## 4.8.1 - Search worker health
Search-index worker health and backlog depth are now visible in the administration diagnostics page.
## Important distinction
A webhook HTTP 503 does not by itself prove a NexaDesk platform incident. Check whether the failure affects one destination or many tenants before escalating.

NexaDesk Cloud Troubleshooting Manual
Synthetic support-engineering knowledge base | Applies primarily to NexaDesk 4.8.x

OAuth Authentication Failures
1. Confirm the token has not expired and inspect issuer and audience claims.
2. Compare application-server time with the identity provider. A difference greater than five minutes can cause otherwise valid tokens to be rejected.
3. If time drift is present, synchronize the host using NTP and restart the authentication worker.
4. Only rotate OAuth credentials after token claims, time synchronization, and identity-provider configuration have been checked.

NexaDesk Cloud Troubleshooting Manual
Synthetic support-engineering knowledge base | Applies primarily to NexaDesk 4.8.x

HTTP 429 / API Throttling
1. Measure requests per minute and concurrent workers for the affected tenant.
2. Check Retry-After response headers where available.
3. Reduce request concurrency and implement exponential backoff with jitter.
4. Do not continuously retry at full speed; this can prolong throttling.

NexaDesk Cloud Troubleshooting Manual
Synthetic support-engineering knowledge base | Applies primarily to NexaDesk 4.8.x

Webhook Delivery Failures
1. Confirm that the customer endpoint is reachable from the public internet.
2. Verify DNS resolution, TLS certificate validity, firewall rules, and endpoint response time.
3. For HTTP 503 responses, verify destination service health first.
4. Inspect the NexaDesk webhook retry queue. Queue saturation across many tenants may indicate a platform-side incident.

NexaDesk Cloud Troubleshooting Manual
Synthetic support-engineering knowledge base | Applies primarily to NexaDesk 4.8.x

Duplicate Ticket Notifications
1. Inspect notification rules for overlapping event conditions.
2. Check whether the same user is subscribed through both an automation rule and a manual subscription.
3. Review recent configuration changes before disabling the notification subsystem.
4. After correcting the duplicate rule, trigger one controlled test ticket and confirm a single delivery.

NexaDesk Cloud Troubleshooting Manual
Synthetic support-engineering knowledge base | Applies primarily to NexaDesk 4.8.x

Delayed Ticket Search
1. Compare the ticket record in the transactional view with search results.
2. Inspect search-index worker health and backlog.
3. Restart a failed indexing worker if required. Rebuilding the entire index should be a last resort.
